title: Remote-admin exposure
context: At LearnTech, the perimeter and internal firewalls run on Fortinet FortiGate, named here only for context. NetShield is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All rule-base data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst reads the firewall rule base when a privileged-access test needs backing up: the review shows who holds access, the rule base shows how they can reach the system.
owner: Your test shows whether LearnTech's privileged-access reviews ran. It does not show how those accounts reach their systems. Before the memo goes, check the Amsterdam firewall: where can admin traffic come from, and does any of it go around the PAM tool? Capture what you find, so I can rely on it without opening the console.
rules: Multi-factor authentication is required for remote, privileged and Tier 3/4 access … Privileged access is held in a privileged-access management (PAM) tool, granted just in time, and recorded where Section 4 requires.
What that means on a firewall
Admin traffic should start at the PAM gateway. A path from anywhere else goes around the PAM tool, and a path from the internet leaves an admin interface reachable from outside.
Exceptions require a documented risk assessment, compensating controls, a named owner, an expiry date (maximum 12 months) and approval per the delegated authority in the GRC Charter Section 6.1.
High = affects a Mission Critical system or no evidence exists. Medium = done late or partly. Low = record-keeping only.

parts.title: Rules that let admin traffic through
parts.ask: Find every rule that lets traffic through on an admin port, and capture exactly those rules.
parts.where: Rules. Use two filters together: one for the kind of traffic, one for what the firewall does with it. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Where each rule's traffic comes from
parts.ask: For each rule you captured, decide where its traffic starts.
parts.where: Rules gives each rule's Source. Objects says what that name contains: read the address, not just the name.

parts.title: Does an exception cover it?
parts.ask: For each rule that does not start at the PAM gateway, decide whether a valid exception covers it.
parts.where: Exceptions lists them by rule. Find the rule, then read its dates against the console's date and against BKB-POL-006 Section 8 in The rules you apply.

parts.title: The one-off that stayed
parts.ask: One of the rules with no valid exception was added for a one-off job and should be gone by now. Find the change that added it, and capture that one row.
parts.where: Change log. Detail says why each rule was added. Filter Event, and Search for the rule's number, so that only its row is left.

parts.title: Rate each one
parts.ask: Rate each rule with no valid exception with rule R26, as you rated deviations in CT-SCRIPT Sheet 3.
parts.where: R26 is in The rules you apply. Objects says what system a rule's Destination is. BKB-ADD-36 Section 8.1 (Policies › Policy Library) says which systems are Mission Critical. Rules' Ticket, Exceptions and Change log show what evidence exists.
